proposal: The Mandate recommends legislation to repeal the federal sugar program and, ideally, the ARC and PLC programs, to stop duplicate ARC/PLC and crop insurance payments in the same year, and to cap the taxpayer share of crop insurance premiums at 50 percent or less. It also urges USDA to refrain from using the Commodity Credit Corporation's discretionary spending authority and Congress to repeal or narrow it.
remaining: Repeal of the federal sugar program (the program was instead extended through crop year 2031).
Repeal of ARC and PLC (the programs were instead reauthorized through 2031 with higher support levels).
A ban on receiving ARC/PLC payments and a crop insurance indemnity in the same year (not found).
A cap of 50 percent or less on the taxpayer share of crop insurance premiums (no cut found).
Repeal or narrowing of CCC section 5 discretionary authority, and USDA refraining from using it.

status_summary: Policy has moved in the opposite direction on the main points. Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) raised ARC/PLC reference prices for crop years 2025 through 2030, raised the ARC guarantee from 86 to 90 percent of benchmark revenue, authorized up to 30 million new base acres, raised the payment limit to $155,000, and extended the sugar program through crop year 2031 with higher loan rates; USDA's rule estimates a 10-year ARC/PLC cost increase of about $46 billion. USDA also established an $11 billion Farmer Bridge Assistance program under section 5(b) of the CCC Charter Act (final rule 2026-02-23), the type of discretionary authority the Mandate advised against using. The House-passed 2026 farm bill makes no change to ARC/PLC covered commodities, and no cut to the general crop insurance premium subsidy rate was found in the provisions reviewed.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed (GovInfo dates it 2025-07-04). Its agriculture provisions (title I, subtitle C) raise ARC/PLC reference prices (section 10301), add up to 30 million base acres (section 10302) and raise the payment limit from $125,000 to $155,000 (section 10307); USDA implemented them in the 2026-01-12 rule below. Its sugar provisions (section 10312) are covered in the 2026-07-09 entry.

FSA and CCC publish the rule implementing the law's ARC, PLC and Dairy Margin Coverage changes: ARC guarantee 90 percent, ARC payment cap 12 percent of benchmark revenue, payment limit $155,000, up to 30 million new base acres; estimated 10-year ARC/PLC cost increase of $46.2 billion.

CCC final rule creates the Farmer Bridge Assistance program, about $11 billion in one-time payments to 2025-crop producers, using section 5(b) of the CCC Charter Act; USDA describes it as a bridge until higher reference-price payments arrive after October 1, 2026.

The House passes H.R. 7567 (224 to 200). Per CRS, it makes no change to the commodities eligible for ARC, PLC or marketing assistance loans, directs the President to prioritize domestic sugar production for domestic food use, and raises premium subsidies for veteran farmers.

The Senate Agriculture chairman releases a discussion draft (Agriculture Act of 2026) that, per CRS, clarifies sugar loan provisions and calls for a study on adding dry edible beans to covered commodities.
CCC final rule implements the law's sugar provisions: program extended from crop year 2025 through 2031 and loan rates raised.

title: Cut farm subsidies (sugar, ARC/PLC, crop insurance) and curb CCC discretionary aid
uncertainties: The specific crop insurance changes in P.L. 119-21 (premium subsidy rates, supplemental coverage options) were not verified from a primary source; the conclusion that the general premium subsidy was not cut rests on CRS statements that the law and farm bill drafts changed crop insurance mainly by expanding it, and on the absence of a cut in the excerpts read. The actual new sugar loan rates were not retrieved. Farm bill action after 2026-07-29 was not checked. A separate specialty crop assistance rule (published 2026-06-01) and the December 2025 announcement of the bridge program were not reviewed. Whether section 5(b) is the exact subsection the Mandate meant by its section 5 discretionary authority is an interpretation.
